Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The method ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?> cls) calls getShortClassName(String className) using cls.getName(). The getShortClassName(String className) method attempts to extract the short class name by parsing the string representation of the class name.

Examining getShortClassName(String className):

- It first returns empty if className is null or empty.
- It contains a comment indicating handling of array encoding, but there is no actual code shown to handle arrays or strip their encoding.
- It finds the last dot index and inner class separator index.
- It extracts a substring after the last dot and replaces inner class separators with package separators.
- The final substring is returned as the short class name.

The current bug report states that when calling getShortClassName with an array class (e.g. String[]), a semicolon is appended incorrectly at the end of the short class name.

The failing test checks getShortClassName(String[].class) expecting "String[]", but the report states that the actual output is "String;" which confirms the semicolon issue.

The problem is that the method getShortClassName(String) does not properly handle array class names. The `Class.getName()` for arrays returns a string with special encoding, e.g. "[Ljava.lang.String;". The current implementation does not strip the "[L" prefix or the trailing ";" suffix specific to array names.

Hence, the root cause is that getShortClassName(String) method lacks proper logic to detect and convert array class names from their JVM notation to a human-readable short name, e.g. "String[]" instead of "String;".

Recent bug reports are not relevant to this particular issue but the current bug report description clearly states the issue that semicolons appear wrongly.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The method ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?> cls) calls getShortClassName(String className) with cls.getName(), but getShortClassName(String) does not specially handle array class names. Array class names in JVM notation have a "[L" prefix and ";" suffix, e.g. "[Ljava.lang.String;" for String array. The method does not strip this encoding and ends up returning names with trailing semicolons like "String;". This causes the test test_getShortClassName_Class to fail when checking for arrays, as the returned short name is incorrect. The lack of handling for array type name representation is the root cause of the bug.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
